header: I kept these helpers small and dependency-free: they cope with a database connection that drops or is replaced while a request is using it. They live apart from index.ts (which imports every entity) so I can test them alone.

symbols.name: TRANSIENT_DB_ERROR
symbols.sig: const TRANSIENT_DB_ERROR = /connection terminated|driver not connected|timeout exceeded|connection timeout|econnreset|server closed the connection| …
doc: I retry only these errors: the pooler dropped a connection, or the pool was replaced mid-request.

symbols.name: withDbRetry
symbols.sig: export async function withDbRetry<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, attempts = 2, delayMs = 250): Promise<T>
doc: I run a database operation and, if it fails with a transient connection error, run it again. `fn` must obtain its connection INSIDE (e.g. `await getDb()` each time) so a retry picks up a fresh, healthy pool. Non-transient errors (bad SQL, constraint violations ...) are thrown immediately and I never retry them.

symbols.name: retireDataSource
symbols.sig: export function retireDataSource( ds: { isInitialized?: boolean; destroy(): Promise<void> }, drainMs = 20_000,): void
doc: I close an old connection pool LATER, not now. In dev, a hot reload replaces the DataSource while requests that started a moment earlier are still running queries on the old one; closing it immediately is what produced "Connection terminated" / "Cannot use a pool after calling end" right after login. So I leave the old pool to finish its work and close it after `drainMs`.
